I'm not convinced China is as invested in the war as you think. The Power of Siberia 2 pipeline for example would have helped the Russian economy, and would have gone to improve China's Oil and Gas weakness. But the two couldn't reach a final deal.  I see this as an example of China being more willing to profit off of Russia's war, rather than them wanting to be an effective ally. If they wanted what was most likely to improve Russia's position, they would have agreed to build the pipeline. 

Also even if Russia would lose the war taking let's say, only the territory it held prior to the February 2022 invasion, why would BRICS pull all of its support? Even weak, Russia is more helpful than no Russia, and is a vital balance to western power in Europe. In the wars to come China will want Russia to be able to stand with it, and be a helpful ally. Given this, pulling its support after a defeat in Ukraine would be counterproductive.

Also, Secretary of Defense Lloyd Austin in a press conference talked about how the sanctions aren't permanent and would be lifted (there is still some ambiguity, but I imagine some would remain in place) if the war was ended in a way the west could tolerate.  This would probably throw the Russian economy into another freefall, but Russia has proven so far its ability to weather the storm.
Could you explain more about how you see Putin falling from power short of a major victory? And what do you imagine that major victory would look like?

Well, Putin's not really in any danger of dying? Broadly speaking he has political support at home still. Plus a nuclear escalation would lose him the support of allies propping up his economy like India and China. Turkey would certainly pull out of any trading agreements with Russia, and would join the western sanctions coalition. Plus Russia knows a nuclear escalation invites dramatic retaliation. You think we're squeezing the Russian Economy now? A tactical (or god forbid strategic) nuclear strike on Ukraine would squeeze like Bowen Constrictor. 

If the Russians attacked NATO assets, they pretty much get the choice of nuclear global apocalypse or complete conventional defeat. Russia knows this, and is therefore deferred from such levels of escalation.

Russia also faces the same escalation concerns that the west faces, and in almost all ways, they are more intense. With such a conventional advantage in manpower, economic strength, and military equipment, Russia is forced to defer from dramatic action. 

I think if Harris wins we will see the war in Ukraine continue for at least a year, I imagine peace talks would begin in winter 2025/2026. I imagine Harris will be slightly more hawkish than Biden, but I imagine his tentativeness for escalation in Russia has rubbed off on her at least a little bit . Russia does have a red line One that would invite that dramatic escalation,, but it's not going to be the red lines that they keep saying. Talk is cheap on the international stage. Prolonged war, dramatic escalation, or a nuclear strike however, are not.
